text:
violet.design: Quick copy + a11y check on the 'Regenerate API key' confirmation. Current copy: 'Are you sure you want to regenerate the API key? Existing clients will stop working.' a11y said the action label is unclear when read standalone. omar.prod: customers get tripped up here. we need to make it explicit that regen rotates the key immediately and that previous key is revoked. Also suggest offering a 'grace period' option if possible. chy.eng: backend note: rotation is immediate; we could implement a 5-minute grace period but its non-trivial and risks security. for now assume immediate revoke. will need a clear warning. jen.a11y: link/button text is announced in isolation by screen readers. 'Regenerate' alone isn't helpful. the confirm button should be a full phrase like 'Regenerate key for service-x' OR pair short visual text with aria-label that includes context. Also the modal should include role=\"alertdialog\" and focus management. violet.design: microcopy proposals (visual vs screen-reader friendly): - Option 1 (visual concise + sr): Visual primary: 'Regenerate key' with aria-label='Regenerate API key for service-x. This will immediately revoke the existing key.' - Option 2 (visual explicit): Primary button: 'Regenerate and revoke old key' - Option 3 (confirm phrase): Change modal to require typing the word 'REGENERATE' and button stays 'Confirm' (helps reduce accidents) Which do folks prefer? omar.prod: Option 1 is sleek, but we must ensure SR users get the full sentence. Option 2 is wordy on the button. Option 3 is heavy friction but might be warranted for orgs with strict security. maybe make Option 3 an admin-level toggle. chy.eng: implementation wise Option 1 is easiest. We can set aria-label attribute on the button to the full sentence. also include a visible one-line caution: 'This will immediately revoke the old key; clients using the old key will fail.' jen.a11y: if you use aria-label, ensure the visible text + aria-label don't contradict. also for keyboard users the modal must announce the caution. aria-describedby on the button pointing to the caution paragraph works well. Example snippet: ```html

This will revoke the existing key immediately. Update clients before regenerating.

``` This keeps the UI concise and accessible. omar.prod: product nit: include the key id in the caution so support tickets have context: 'This will revoke key id abc123.' But avoid showing full key. show truncated id with aria-label exposing full id if necessary. violet.design: updated microcopy plan: - Modal body: one-line caution with id=regen-caution: 'This will revoke API key abc1***** and stop any clients using it.' - Visual primary: 'Regenerate key' - Visual secondary: 'Cancel' - Accessibility: button has aria-describedby=\"regen-caution\" and the modal uses role=\"alertdialog\". For extra safety, admin orgs will get an opt-in 'Require confirmation phrase' toggle. chy.eng: noted. well implement aria-describedby and truncated id display. also add title attr with full key id on hover for admins. jen.a11y: final checklist: confirm button has descriptive name in context via aria-describedby or aria-label, modal uses alertdialog, focus trapped and returned, caution announced via aria-live if appropriate, test with NVDA/VoiceOver. Also ensure color contrast for danger button and focus ring visible. infra-bot: rotation-job 2026-03-23T14:02:11Z queued for key abc1***** by user omar.prod. omar.prod: thanks everyone. violet, can you push the Figma update and I'll sign off? let's add a small analytics event on 'regenerate_confirmed' to track accidental regens. violet.design: will do 4aa i'll post the figma link and the new copy tokens in #design-docs when ready.
